article.title: AIP-180: Backwards compatibility
article.abstract: The article introduces AIP-180, which outlines guidelines for ensuring backwards compatibility in API design. It covers principles and best practices to maintain existing functionality while introducing changes.

newConcepts.definition: Ensuring that changes to an API or system do not break existing functionality, allowing smooth transitions and maintaining compatibility with existing code.
A set of guidelines and best practices for designing APIs, ensuring consistency, clarity, and maintainability in API development.
The principles and practices for creating effective, maintainable, and scalable APIs that meet the needs of developers and users.
A widely used language for technical documentation, APIs, and software development.
